previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 11%, chronic graft-versus-host disease, bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia, and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, was admitted for rectal pain and chills. He presented with hypotension and an elevated lactate, consistent with septic shock. Imaging revealed a new 5.4 cm perianal abscess, which was drained at the bedside by colorectal surgery. His infection resolved with source control, and antibiotics were discontinued. He had an episode of vomiting attributed to calcium acetate, which was switched to sevelamer. He remained stable on his home oxygen and continued his regular dialysis schedule. His condition improved, and he was discharged home with follow-up arranged, new medication instructions, and guidance on weight monitoring and symptom reporting.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with history of AML 
(in remission s/p bone marrow transplant in ___, disease 
complicated by GVHD with BOOP and anthracycline-induced 
biventricular congestive heart failure with an EF 10%,ESRD on HD 
via port MWF ___ -___, history of perirectal 
abscess who presents with two-day history of weakness, nausea, 
vomiting, diarrhea, found to have fever concerning for 
gastrointestinal illness.

ACTIVE ISSUES: 
===============
#Viral Gastroenteritis: The patient's presentation of acute 
onset N/V/D in the setting of recent exposure to grandchildren 
with viral illness was most concerning for viral gastroenteritis 
such as norovirus. He was initially hypotensive and symptomatic, 
detailed below, likely due to hypovolemia. Given his 
immunocompromised state, initial blood cultures were drawn and 
he was intended to have stool studies. However, his N/V/D 
completely resolved within 24 hours of admission and he was 
tolerating PO intake well. As such, these studies were never 
sent. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with 
his PCP shortly after leaving the hospital.

#Hypotension: The patient has baseline, asymptomatic low blood 
pressures on multiple prior hospitalizations, while 
asymptomatic. However, this admission, he was found to have 
SBP's in the ___ with symptoms of hypovolemia and 
hypoperfusion. As such, he was given fluid resuscitation, with 
care not to generate iatrogenic fluid overload given his anuric 
status with good effect. He was discharged with BP's consistent 
with prior baseline without any further symptoms.

CHRONIC ISSUES: 
==========================
#ESRD on HD: The patient is anuric and receives MWF hemodialysis 
via his tunneled HD line. He was continued on his home 
supplements and underwent dialysis on ___ as he missed his 
scheduled dialysis appointment on ___ in the setting of 
presenting to the ED.

# Chemotherapy-induced Cardiomyopathy: The patient has a known 
anthracycline induced cardiomyopathy with EF 10% as recently as 
___. He was slightly hypervolemic on admission with increased 
O2 requirement, likely secondary to fluid resuscitation. 
However, he tolerated dialysis well with post-HD weight 
consistent with prior d/c weights. He was not started on an ACEi 
or Beta Blocker due to his low baseline blood pressures.

#AML s/p BMT, complicated by GVHD: The patient is in remission 
after transplant and did not have symptoms of active GVHD this 
admission, apart from COP as detailed below.

#Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia: The patient has a history of 
COP, likely as a result of GVHD. He was initially up to 4L on 
supplemental O2, but quickly de-escalated to his home 3L NC 
after HD. He was continued on his home prednisone 2mg PO daily 
with ppx on Bactrim and acyclovir (in lieu of valacyclovir due 
to formulary restrictions).

#Sarcoidosis: The patient was continued on his home prednisone 
and ppx as above.

#Pancytopenia: The patient presented with anemia and 
thrombocytopenia, mild and stable, consistent with prior values. 
These were felt to be likely the result of damage to marrow from 
prior chemotherapy and BMT in addition to ESRD.

====================
